transcript.text:
I can help with that. When a tumble dryer appears not to work, it usually comes down to one of three things: it isn't getting power (like a tripped fuse or loose plug), the door isn't latched securely so the safety switch won't engage, or a programme setting is preventing it from starting. To narrow this down quickly:
1. Check if the display lights up when you turn the dial.
2. Ensure the door is pushed in firmly until it clicks.
3. Try selecting a standard 'Cottons' or 'Mixed Load' cycle and pressing start. Let me know what happens with these steps.
Lights come on but nothing happens when I press start. The door doesn't click shut, it swings back slightly open. Door had felt loose for a few days.

That suggests the issue: because the door isn't latching securely, the safety switch never engages, so the machine refuses to start. This points strongly to a worn or broken plastic catch on the door itself, rather than an electrical fault with the switch. Please unplug the dryer first, then inspect the catch mechanism for any visible cracks or breakage and tell me what you see.
Unplugged it. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, I found the piece on the floor. If I hold the door shut and press start it runs, stops when I let go.

That suggests the cause. The dryer won't start because the safety interlock isn't engaged when the door is released. Once installed, ensure it clicks firmly shut; if it does, the dryer will work normally again.
Not sure what you mean by "once installed" - do I need to buy a new door catch? What should I do next?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
Yes, you will need to buy a new plastic catch (often called a door handle or tongue) to fix this properly. Since it has snapped off, holding the door shut is only a temporary workaround and not safe for regular use. To help you find the exact part, could you please tell me your tumble dryer's make and model number? This is usually on a sticker inside the door frame or around the opening.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Hotpoint. I don't know the model number offhand, but I can have a look inside the door recess if that's where it is. Will check now.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
That is perfect. Please go ahead and find the model number on that sticker inside the door recess or around the opening. Once you have it, let me know exactly what it says (it usually starts with letters like TDC, WML, etc., followed by numbers). With that, I can tell you exactly which replacement part you need to buy so you can fix this properly.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Ok, I've had a look inside the door recess but I can't find the model number yet. Where exactly should I be looking?

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
The model number is usually on a sticker inside the door frame or around the opening. If you can't see it there, check behind the lint filter or on the back of the machine. Since we have confirmed the plastic tongue has snapped off and that is why the dryer won't start, this is a mechanical fault requiring a replacement part. You will need to buy a new door catch/tongue for your Hotpoint tumble dryer. Once you find the model number, search for 'Hotpoint [model] door handle' or 'door catch' at an appliance parts retailer. Install it according to the instructions (usually just clipping into place), and the machine should work normally again.
